newsitem.title: UK: Athens bourse close highlights risk for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse close highlights risk for foreigners.

text.p: Analysts in London expressed dismay on Wednesday at the three-day closure of the Athens bourse, saying it underlined the riskiness of the Greek market for international investors.
"It shows that the stock market is for all intents and purposes very much an emerging market," said Michael Harris, equity analyst at Merrill Lynch.
The Athens bourse closed on Friday following the failure of a small brokerage firm, Delta Securities, to pay 2.6 billion drachmas ($10.94 million) in settlements last week.
It reopened for trading late on Wednesday morning, although only selected brokers were authorised to trade by the exchange.
"It is just not something you would expect," said Danielle Downing of Salomon Brothers. "It's unusual because in comparison to other markets like Poland and Russia, Greece is much more developed."

The Athens bourse has a market capitalisation more than three times Poland's stock market. After surpassing the 1,000 level in March, the exchange has fallen more than 10 percent and is currently trading near January levels. Analysts and investors expressed surprise at the extent and duration of the problems at the bourse and said it signaled lack of a proper regulatory structure in Greece.
"I was quite surprised...that this sort of level of losses could be sustained without anybody knowing anything about it," said Radhika Ajmera, director of Abtrust Fund Managers.
"The fact that a small broker effectively goes bust is no surprise, but the reponse to it showed they had no mechanism for dealing with it," Harris said.
A mature market would have moved on rather than been dragged down and forced to close, he said.
Analysts said they had expected the closure to last at most a day, rather than drag on through the weekend to Wednesday.
"I thought it would last a maximum of a day, but the problems of settlement are much deeper than people had anticipated," Ajmera said.
Analysts felt the incident would have a negative short term impact, but said investors generally viewed the Greek market tentatively and this would only reinforce that outlook.
Harris said that while Merrill was already underweight in Greece, potential investors who had become interested in the country following the recent elections may re-evaluate.
"The market will restabilise, probably at a lower level," Harris said.
"We very much view it as an emerging market anyway," Ajmera said. "These are obviously risks you associate with an emerging market."
The Athens general share index closed down 1.35 percent on Wednesday or 12.39 points lower at 908.42.
